       Once Sul slew King Zzvfur with the Fierce Axe, the Duergar armies were quick to withdraw back into the Underdark. The duergar refused to bend the knee to the Overlight dwur but they acknowledged the cessation of hostilities. The duergar of the Barrier Peaks, Death Cultists and loyal to neither dwur faction, were forced into exile. Unwelcome both below and above ground, these dwarves moved into Western Oerik or south into the Amedio Jungle and the Hepmonaland.
   Sul (who never dreamed of this day) took the Fierce Axe into the Sulhauts where he became High Lord of the Oerik Dwur. Not a king, for the title had been abolished on the continent. Sul did make overtures with the dwur kingdom of Rockhome in Mystara to recognise the authority of the High Lord but, as expected, Rockhome maintained their independence.
   While the dwur celebrated their victory, the majority of the Flannaes were still engulfed in war. The orcish armies of Gruumsh had slowed somewhat in their advance after the loss of two important generals and the wounding of Gruumsh himself..yet the forces were immense and reinforcements continued gating in from many worlds.
   Much of the central Flannaes were humanoid occupied and the inhabitants found themselves enslaved, starved and in constant peril, but strong resistance remained in parts of the Adri, Sunndi and south and west of the Dreadwood. Despite their promised hero not coming to their aid, the good allies Ye'Cind, Ulla, Lord Dueillig, Heward, Yolanda and Garl Glittergold were stalwart in defence of the Flannaes, sacrificing their own pleasures in their determination to restore their lands to goodness. Caowyn and the other tuatha de dannan recovered somewhat from their mysterious illness but they were diminished and their weapons and armour had lost some of their magic. Their time had passed.
    Demi-human allies led by elven god Corellon Larethian (and the spirit of Moradin) continued to frustrate the Gruumsh occupation of Toril but Corellon knew more needed to be done, risks must be taken. On the distant worlds of the tentacled, abarrent Illithids, feared as Mind Flayers, amongst that darkness, new opportunities were arising... See less

   Uklinigo made it up to the Fourth Landing where he chose to have a short rest. The mind flayer had brought a little snack of brain jerky which his twitching pink tentacles eagerly grabbed and devoured. The Fourth Landing was a solidly constructed alcove between fleets of steps. There was a small library with rather dry literature and a stunning silver and black onyx bas-relief on the far wall representing the undersea union between the jelly-like aboleths and the enormous krakens.  Uklinigo had forgotten who had carved it, but he felt happy when he gazed upon the scene and decided to look it up once he returned to his master.
   After climbing another thirty or so steps, Uklinigo felt a cold and sticky hand touch the nape of his naked neck, just above his robe. He turned about and saw on the step below him a gaunt, tall, wrinkled and pale yellow figure with matted black hair reaching out to touch him again 
   What was a Block 3 Subliminal doing here?  The thin bipedal humanoid was miles from its quarters. Uklinigo stretched out his tentacles and blasted out a psychic crush. The Block 3 Subliminal shrieked and bolted down the steps. 
   Silly, confused creature, thought Uklinigo as he watched the thing flee out of sight. He turned back to the journey up the steps..
   At last, he reached the old dusty chambers of the old library. Uklinigo saw books on shelves, marble desks and various scientific contraptions, long abandoned. The young mind flayer went to the shelves looking for the book he needed. Absorbed with his task, Uklinigo did not see a pale, blue ghostly form of an elven maiden clutching the beating heart of her dead lover in her left hand, floating across the room with the visage of raw hatred across her face. She reached the far double doors and shrieked.
   Uklinigo looked up and saw the ghost. He shook uncontrollably, yet mastered his fear and  determined to blast the phantom back to hell. 
   The doors creaked open, and emerging from the darkness beyond were sixteen, seventeen, no, eighteen gaunt, pale lemon, wrinkled and matted Block 3 Subliminals, rushing across to the mind flayer in pure rage... See less

   Win-Daled was reaching the end of her mortal life.  She had ruled Risewater, home of the Suloise, for many years and the population had  increased,  with further settlements to the North and West.. But the East was off limits, too close to the  Singing Lands.
   Most of her tenure as Suel Chief had been relatively easy. Win-Daled was by far the greatest Arch-mage in the nation, and she had the mighty elven Ye'Cind and the great Flan wunderkind Heward as friends and advisors. 
 The Singing One and the Flan roguish  warrior were fond of wandering though, and lately had been frequenting Risewater less and less. Ye'Cind was still a young elf maiden and Heward seemed to have stopped aging at forty.
    Win-Daled herself felt old, and she was ready to move on to the next stage of existence.She had hoped Heward would take up the job...oh well...his dalliances with the nymphs, dryads and other feminine creatures of Fey was apparently taking up too much of his time for serious work.
    Therefore, Win-Daled chose the son of a gallant former bandit to be her successor. Gryman was intelligent, contemplative and had earned the respect of many of the young Suel in his twenty three years. He was deeply moved by the honour, and promised to serve the Suel faithfully and fairly. Win-Daled assured him that she knew he would.
   At the end of the year, after giving a last speech and wishing everybody well, Win-Daled clutched her heart and fell back on the stage. Her face was serene, and her lips curved with the hint of a smile. She never rose again.
   52 SD, Ye'Cind finally joined up with a small grey elf community that had splintered off from Celene and helped to found a new Elven nation north of the Vast swamp.

Hail the Chief 
   Baron Smoler had wanted to lead the attack upon Rhaan but his advisors cautioned against this. What if the city was better defended than expected, or what would become of the realm if by some freak chance, an arrow caught him in the throat or an eye? The fire giant infantry was the best in the world. Let them do their job.
   Smoler had agreed and now he regretted it. He had moved down into the Suel plains to get as close as possible without being drawn into the combat, and he quickly found that he couldn't see anything but the backs of the giants. The king had generously offered his Baron his personal guards of honour, and they were freaks, some reaching upward of eighteen feet high. Their armour was garish and ceremonial, and to make themselves even bigger their hats were heaped up masses of cave bear fur. They seemed barely trained with their great swords, holding them awkwardly, and their gangly bodies were shaped like stalks, and their square, elongated heads made them top heavy. 
   What made them far worse was that they completely blocked Smoler's view. He was ignominiously forced to retreat into the foothills where at least now he could see. Unfortunately, he felt incredibly distant from the melee unfolding below, and his dashing cloak of white furred snow serpent, his scale mail fashioned from hatchling silver dragons, and his mirrored sword seemed faintly ridiculous now. 
   The combatants might as well have been beetles or ants, so distant were they, but at least Smoler could make out the gist of the battle. It was going almost as well as he had expected, though one Suel magi and a few priests had bolstered the defenders (fortuitously only bringing down a couple of the King's guards) for a brief moment before being cut down. 
   Soon it was all over. His fire giants were victorious. The city fell to Baron Smoler.
                              *****
   Smoler entered the smouldering city and was at a loss of what to do with all of the Suel humans. Their were lots of old men, and boys, and thousands of women, girls and little children. Why hadn't they all fought like fire giants did when their halls were invaded? And they all chattered and yelped and wept with cries worse than giant goats. Smoler couldn't understand a word, but fortunately one of his advisors spoke Suel, and he was able to interpret.
   "They beg for their lives," said the advisor.
   "Do they think us barbarians?" exclaimed Smoler, "There is no honour in slaying non-combatants without good reason. Some we will take as slaves, of course. The rest...what do we do with them?"
   "We must organise them by sex. Males and females don't tend to like being heaped up all together. We should separate them and make them swear fealty to our King."
   Baron Smoler nodded in agreement.
                                  ****
   The city had a new name. Smoler, it was called, and the new province was called Kash in honour of the Baron's late father. Many Suel had left, but some had stayed in return for obedience and safety. There was a knock on the door.
   The Black Monks had arrived.
                                  ****
   Baron Smoler was extremely drunk. He staggered about, dishevelled, unshaven and undignified. He didn't care. Vecna's Eye was upon him. The city was not called Smoler. The province was not called Kash. The conquered little realm was Vecna's.
   Vecna offered up his Hand in friendship, the Black Monks had said, and it would be a shame to feel the back of it. See less

A Funeral 
   Empress Gubudilana lay in her casket.  Bishop Nam-ko of the Order of Syrul supervised her placement into the golden carriage. The titanotheres were hitched up, and the procession was ready to begin.
   The Gargoyle Palace loomed above the mourners like a mountain. Somewhere within, Syrul was inside. Nam-ko turned to the Palace and bowed reverently. The blight that had befallen the Suel had even penetrated this holy place. The Skulks were everywhere, cowardly murderers who slew the good and dear. The greatest scions of the Imperium had vanished from the world. 
   Bishop Nam-ko bowed because she knew that Syrul was as appalled as she was. The goddess had chosen Gubudilana to rule the Imperium, but the cursed Wee Jas and her followers, corrupted by the impurity of the Zindians, would rather bring everything down than submit to the true Suel.
   The carriage began to move, the procession shuffling after it. With Empress Gubudilana gone, only one Emperor remained. The Emperor of the haunted Drow lands. The land of the betrayer, Wee Jas. Nam-ko returned to her position at the head of the crowd, her red gold symbol of a forked tongue raised so that everyone could see that Syrul was with them.
   The gravesite was beneath a natural slab of quartz surrounded by sweet smelling berry bushes. The hole had been dug, and two lesser clerics of Syrul waited there. The titanotheres pushed through thickets blocking the path, then the carriage emerged, bright and light on such a gloomy day. Bishop Nam-ko stepped forward to her comrades, and conversed with them briefly.  The titanotheres halted near the hole, then slaves brought down the casket, then carried it to the hole. As they gathered together the ropes and hoist, Nam-ko began the service.
   "How can this be?" she asked the mourners, "how can Syrul let our Imperium fall to the dark plots of Wee Jas?" Nam-ko paused, watching for reactions in the crowd. Many were sobbing, but others were yelling in anger, cursing Wee Jas and the Skulks.
   "Our Empress, Gubudilana of House Crix has indeed left us for her new journey," continued Nam-ko, "and with her death, the war is over."
   Cries of outrage. Roars of despair.
   "Hush, children, hush! Do you not yet understand the wisdom of Syrul? She herself will take Wee Jas to task. She herself has tasted the bitter salts of Wee Jas and her Zindia. The day dawns, shines and dims. The night shadows, glooms and glimmers. What is up comes down and what is down never forgets. Children, we are all Suel. Our day has darkened into night, and we have all fallen down. We lay the true Empress to rest, and we put away our arms. Calm shall return to the Imperium, and we must repose as our Empress must repose. But children, Suel, brothers and sisters of Syrul, we shall never forget who we are. We are of the Imperium and one day we will seize it utterly!" See less

Assassins among us!
1711 SD
   Assassins were among us!  Emperor Poul of the Zelred House knew that the Skulks were here. They hadn't been seen, but they had been felt. Every night one less noble had woken up. The Skulks were playing with him. 
   Emperor Poul decided to seal his personal rooms. Let no one in or out. What about food, and water? He could live upon conjured food and water. Conjured food was dry and fairly bland, but he would cope. And his stockpile of liqueur was within his chambers . 
   Emperor Poul of the Zelred was the true ruler of the Suel Imperium and nothing was going to stop him from fulfilling his destiny, and certainly not the magically created Skulks.
                                 *****
   Cenc saw Emperor Poul pouring himself a stiff drink. She saw him because she was in the room with him. She crouched on-top of a shelf of scrolls, unheard and unseen. A poisoned dagger was at her belt. He was sealing all of the doors. Even if he had beaten her to it,  closed off the rooms before the Skulks could get in, it wouldn't have saved him. The magician, Jaspi would have broken the locks. 
                                  *****
   Another false emperor eliminated. Another step closer to the end of the war. Why should the common soldiers die for the dreams of the elite? All of the Suel houses were fighting for the glory of the already glorious. Cenc was enjoying herself. The taking of lives of those that had never even seen her to look down on her was surprisingly easy. She supposed it was because she didn't see them as people. 
   The high Lords and Ladies, draped in red and white and gold, jostling for Themselves.
   They called themselves Suel and Human.
   Cenc was a Skulk. No longer a Suel, and no longer a human. She was an invisible assassin, as were all of her friends, murdering in order to save lives.
   Human lives. Suel lives.
   Cenc knew that she was a monster. It would be better for the Noble Houses to realise that they were only monsters too. See less

Religious Fervour in Silver Land
1710 SD
   The elves of Silver Land in north west Mystara had become very unruly. Lord Kint put down the latest report. Wasn't he a reasonable man? The elves wanted nice homes and nice food, so didn't it then make sense to do what you are told? Capricious, foolish creatures.
   Another crackdown was in order. Lord Kint went down a couple of flights of stairs then opened up the secret door behind the last step. The room beyond was tiny and pitch black, but Lord Kint was a lich, transformed by Vecna after some heart troubles, and darkness had no effect upon his vision. There was another concealed door in the far wall. This door opened up into what was little more than a secret shelf. And on the shelf was a jar. A jar that contained a heart. Lord Kint's old, mortal heart. Lord Kint pulled out the jar, then held it close to his cold, undead chest. It was comforting to him to do this, especially when he was forced to conduct nasty business, and lately he had been forced to conduct a lot of nasty business. 
                               *****
   An hour later, Lord Kint returned to the administrative centre feeling much more calm and focused. He summoned his General. 
   The aide was extremely agitated, "the General isn't available. I cannot reach him."
   "What do you mean?" demanded Kint, "you gave me that report yourself. The elves are religious fanatics. They refuse to work the mines, and they cry out for their Messiah. They even threaten to summon their god Corellon Larethian. They must be punished with military action. Five percent must die."
   Of course the aide knew all that, but he still hasn't been able to contact the General. 
   "Well then, who have you been able to contact?"
   The aide ran off to do whatever he could. He returned a few minutes later with a brand new report. Lord Kint took it from him roughly then quickly perused the contents. His grey face turned white. The elves would have to wait. Arik had made his move. The General was already making his way to the border with his best soldiers to defend Silver Land. Arik the half golem rebel had finally struck, his kodge army crossing the river. 
   The war had begun. See less

1065 SD
   Lolth had known fear.
    Her mother was the Queen of Chaos, and her brother was Miska the Wolf Spider, so yes, she had known fear. The three of them together...it had been tense.
   Lolth had been alone now for a long time, so the emotion that coursed through her demonic body was not welcome. She and her Singing Ones had flourished in the rainforests and cities southwest of the Hellfurnaces, they were unassailable. Even as the Death Cults encroached, Lolth had triumphed.
   Then the rumours came, Tharizdun had found the Throne of the Gods.
   What was this Throne? Why hadn't she heard of it? 
   The rumours were soon confirmed. The greatest dragon on Oerik had fallen to Tharizdun and his Throne.
   Then, some of her Singing Ones were taken by Tharizdun, even her favourite handmaiden, Elehonna. 
   Lolth had to find a way to defend herself and her people.
   Lolth had once possessed the Scroll of Vile Darkness, and she had studied it much before it had been snatched from her grasp. 
   She remembered something, there may be a way to shield the Singing Ones from Tharizdun,
            **************************** 
   Lolth found  a series of caverns and tunnels snaking under the Hellfurnaces, a quiet branch of the Underdark. 
   In her spider form she sprayed webs over the whole place. When she finally finished, she chanted the spells that would turn the sticky webs into a silvery shield, a shield that would block Tharizdun's mental intrusion.
         *****************************
   "Aren't I beautiful?"
   Lolth knew that she was beautiful. She had assumed the form of an indigo elf, stunning but also forbidding. She was draped in jewels and wore little else. 
    Lolth asked the Singing Ones to come with her, under the mountains. Follow their Queen, their Mother, their Lover. 
   I know you love the forests, the sun and the moons, she said. I know you love the cities that you have built, the art you have made, the vistas of the World.
   I know you don't wish to be cave dwellers like the duergar. But Tharizdun stalks the land. Tharizdun wants to take you away from me. 
O, my Children!
   It will only be for a short time. I shall soon set forth to destroy Tharizdun myself.
   In the meantime, be good little children, obey your Spider Mother. Take what you can carry if you must, but come quickly or Tharizdun will find you.
         ******************************
   The majority of the Singing Ones did follow Lolth under the mountains. There were some who resisted. Elves who liked the good life too much, or feared the Underdark, or didn't take the stories about Tharizdun seriously.
   Lolth didn't argue with those that wished to stay. Let them. What did she care? She was only interested in preserving those that were most loyaL
   Lolth had no idea how to stop Tharizdun. She had no plans, she feared him, feared that he would seek her out and make her his slave. So she chose to hide.
   How long she would hide she didn't know. Maybe Tharizdun would move on, leave Oerth and wander other Planes. Maybe some heroes would best him.
   She could hope. But she would not hide forever. In the Underdark she would discover a way to make her elves stronger, fiercer, ruthless.
   One day, she and her new elves would return.
             **************************
      Tharizdun was looking out into the dark ribbon of night for his throne sat upon a ledge open to the sky. 
   He saw  a few twinkling stars, and, a rare event,  both moons. 
   They were far away, but they seemed so close! Tharizdun felt his power growing day by day. The Throne made his ethereal neurones thrum.
   Perhaps he could reach out and touch one of the moons?
   Tharizdun concentrated hard, stretched his insubstantial essence across the cosmos,and pushed the moons. They spun erratically for a moment, then Sol's gravity caught them, brought them back into orbit.
   Although the Sun was on the other side of Oerth, he could feel its anger.
   There was a Power there, in Sol, watching him. 
   Suddenly Tharizdun could feel the weight of worlds, and his tendrils stretched, frayed, split.
   His ethereal essence was disrupted, Sol was reaching for him, trying to grab him, reel him in.
   No! 
   Tharizdun relaxed and let himself go. Like a spent elastic band, his insubstantial mass returned to his vaporous body. 
   He was safe on the Throne.
   what was that god in the Sun? How long until he could reach out and bring the Sun down?
   What could be done to boost his power still further? Tharizdun was unnassilable on the Throne, but he wanted so much more. He wanted to touch the Universe, and he was so close...
            *********************
   Within his mists, the Scroll of Vile Darkness, now incorporeal, grew in power also, affected by the Throne.  The scroll was in a state of ecstatic exaltation, absorbing Darkness and Despair, probing the Hidden Reaches that before was known only to the Throne of the Gods.
   The Scroll of Vile Darkness felt the new spells churning within itself, and, with gratitude to its greatest Master, shared its newfound knowledge with Tharizdun. There was a way to stretch across the Universe. Even the Multiverse. Listen to me, Dear Tharizdun. I will lead you on a dance, you and me! We shall twist together, and twist reality itself!
  All Hail Dread Tharizdun! See less

   It was a well known fact that a ghost of an elvish female haunted the upper labyrinths of the vault. She had been seen on many occasions, a young, beautiful, pale elf maiden, clutching in her ghostly left hand a beating heart, said to be all that was left of her lover. She wailed and shrieked when no one was listening and wandered aimlessly and intermittently. Many years would go by with no sound or sighting, only for the ghost to appear again and roam the old chambers, unnerving the visitors to the upper levels.
   Encounters with the ghost stretched back thousands of years. She was said to be an early victim of the Illithids, the Mind Flayers, who had abducted her and her lover from Oerik just after the Dragon Times. Nobody living remembered her alive and her name (and that of her lover) was entirely forgotten. It was said that even the phantom herself had failed to remember her name or even why she held on to the beating heart of her dead soul mate.
   Ghosts were not unknown in Mind Flayer society. When strong psionic powers gather together (as the Illithids did in their underground cities), the minds of the victims, once devoured, sometimes remained as a psychic imprint, a harmless yet curious bi- product that faded away after a few centuries. This ghost was different, she seemed to be dimly aware of her surroundings and when she encountered an Illithid, well dressed humanoids with heads that vaguely resembled a mauve and pink octopus, her pretty face would contort into a mask of resentment and rage. So strong was the radiant emotion that the sensitive Mind Flayer would forget what item or book they were looking for in the upper labyrinth,  lose interest in eating brains and become anaemic and weak. 
   The ghost of the female elf maiden was therefore one to avoid and fear. The young neophyte Uklinigo knew the stories well and always planned to avoid the largely uninhabited upper levels of the vault, but unfortunately his master, Arch-Flayer Glinggatur, was sure an important book he needed for his splicing experiments was located in one of the upper libraries. Uklinigo was tasked to fetch the book despite it being known that the ghost had been particularly active lately. Glinggatur was not very impressed with the neophyte because there was never reward without risks, as his highly rewarding experiments with the Block 3 Subliminals could attest. Therefore, Uklinigo made his way up the fleets of steps that led to the 5th Library where the book was said to be located, despite his trepidation... See less

Boy Wonder (1)
1722 SD
   The harpies were wreaking havoc in the villages skirting the Gambodge forest. The Empire was angry, and Vecna had stretched out his Hand. Woodcutters were plucked into the sky and devoured. Wandering travellers were lost. Ur Flan were making their presence felt too, and many people suspected of being in league with the rebels were rounded up and taken to the Isles of Woe. 
   Culber had managed to evade these myriad difficulties, but it had made her extra cautious, and she was forced to stop her smuggling operation. What had made Vecna so angry? The speculation was that his loss of his Mystaran province to the rebel Arik had hit him hard, both personally and economically. Stories were that the Glantri Empire, his supposed ally, wasn't picking sides, and the island of Kodge Land between Oerik and Mystara was wavering, and Vecna's Hand there was losing its grip. 
   Whatever the truth was, the dark times had become even darker. Culber and the Gavronites met extremely infrequently, and isolated, they felt helpless to fight on. Culber knew that even Celene was losing its light. Ur Flan surrounded their borders and trade with the kingdom, nefarious though it was, was almost totally ended. 
   Then there was the boy. He was four or five, his skin like dark copper, his hair black and curly. His eyes were pale and green, and he was staring at Culber like a cat.
   It was very disconcerting. What did the little boy want?
   His mother was laughing. They were preparing a meal when the boy had come in then stood, staring., "Don't mind him. He always does that."
   Culber frowned, "he should be with the other children."
   The mother gave a helpless smile, "the other children hate him "
   "I can see why," said Culber, "he is very rude."
   The boy belched.
   "Is he a simpleton?" continued Culber, "you had best hide him. The Ur Flan will kill him."
   "I am not a simpleton," announced the boy, "I just find you fascinating."
   The mother had stopped laughing. She gave her boy a smack. "Leave us! Go and play somewhere else."
   The little boy shrugged. He turned to go, then strained his neck, and looked Culber in the eye, "I don't want to be here. You have taken other children away. Take me too."
   Culber went red, "whatever are you talking about? I am a laundress. I don't take children anywhere."
   The boy went back into the little kitchen. "When I was one year old, you took Fulig to Celene. When I was two, my mother helped you  take Hulli and Sibby there as well. And there were others. These are the ones I knew."
   "How could you know that?" exclaimed Culber.
   "Fulig used to cuddle me when I was in my crib. Hulli and Sibby gave me sweets and told me that I would grow up to be a wizard!"
   "But how can you remember them? You were too young."
   "What do you mean, Culber? I remember when I was born. The two moons were out and mother was crying. It was a little bit disorientating, if I am being honest."
   Culber looked at astonishment at the boy's mother, who was clearly embarrassed.
   "Your child isn't a simpleton, I take that back, but he is in even more danger than before. If Vecna finds out about him..."
   "I know," interrupted the boy, "that's why you have to smuggle me across the border. Please. I can feel great good within you. I will go now, but I will be back in seven days. Have a plan by then." He turned to his mother as he went to leave, "sorry, Mother." See less

   Some two hundred miles west of the Crystalmists was a large lake, today known as Lake Udrukankar. Several rivers flowed into it,  all but one nowadays reduced to dry dust. 
   Baklindi traders and fishermen sailed the lake on simple barges and rafts and canoes.
   The land about the lake, now the Dry Steppes, were fertile grass and woodlands. Living amongst the Baklindi were cat people, centaurs, Jann and gnolls. 
   The Baklindi were emerging from their dark era as slaves to the Vaati and they feared outsiders.
   Outsiders came, and the Baklindi were right to be afraid.
   Thousands, tens of thousands, men, women, elves, halflings, clothed in many different ways, in many different styles, descended upon the north eastern bank of the lake. Their breath was a white mist of frost, and its touch burned skin and cracked wood. 
   Barges sunk, Baklindi fell to hyperthermia.
   That is, those Baklindi that didn't suddenly join the ranks of the invaders and strike out at their kin with the same cold mist. 
   The bank secured, some invaders stayed at the lake, many others retreated east into the Crystalmists.
   They crossed to the other side, fewer in number, but with large numbers of hill, stone, frost and storm giants. 
   Across the Sheldomar valley they now went. 
   There were still Singing One settlements here, those that chose to defy the will of Lolth. 
   Most joined the ranks of the eastward travellers.
   Ulaa had sent troops into the Sheldomar since the majority of the Singing One elves had  disappeared. The half dwarf had hoped to resettle the good people back into their former homes, but reports came back to her that was not good news.
   Hundreds of thousands of people of differing cultures and species had gathered here, moving north, east and west. They never spoke, never rested, never ate. 
   Some were Undead.
   All were Tharizdun.
   We follow those that came into the valley from the Crystalmists. They continued east, crossing into Celene, felling elven archers with their frost.  Corellon Larethian protected the main towns and the eerie travellers skirted them and pushed into the Suss forest.
   Emerging from the Suss, they headed towards the Drachensgrabs, to Tharizdun's birth place.
   The travellers, now long dead  and animated as zombies by Tharizdun, reached a cave then stood outside its entrance, rigid and still.
   An enormous glowing dragon emerged from the cave, floating several feet off the ground, translucent and silent. 
   The Ghost Dragon smiled when she saw the gathered mass of zombies, giants amongst them. Her son had done well.
   The zombies then entered the cave, then came out again some minutes later with pieces of ghostly stone. 
They then turned west, going back the way they had come. See less
